thread:
alex: FYI ran into a nasty thing when trying to deploy our example mono repo to Edge (Next edge runtime). The SDK works in node dev but the edge bundle fails to resolve the package.json exports when pnpm creates the .pnpm symlink layout.

alex: error from next build: 
```
Failed to compile.
Could not resolve 'node_modules/@redwood/sdk' from '/workspace/apps/web/src/edge.ts'
(rollup plugin) Error: Cannot read package.json for '@redwood/sdk'
```

nora: that's the classic symlink + exports issue. Which bundler/runtime? Next edge uses esbuild under the hood for the edge function. Esbuild won't always follow symlinks to read package.json exports unless the path looks like a real package.

ben: did you try adding the package to next.config.js transpilePackages? sometimes forcing transpile makes it bundle the actual files instead of relying on exports resolution. We use: 
```js
// next.config.js
module.exports = {
  transpilePackages: ['@redwood/sdk'],
};
```

alex: tried transpilePackages, Next started bundling but then TS types vanished — tsc/IDE couldn't find types for the SDK. Locally node resolution ok, but vscode intellisense broke in the app workspace.

nora: types issue is probably because the editor resolves types through the workspace layout. Quick fixes: 
- add a types field pointing to an explicit file in the exports (e.g. "types": "dist/index.d.ts")
- or add a top-level types entry in a lightweight wrapper package in the root, then point your app to that package.

ben: also worth checking pnpm's public-hoist-pattern in .npmrc. If you add: 
```
public-hoist-pattern=@redwood/*
```
it will hoist the package to node_modules where builders commonly expect package.json to live. Less invasive than switching node-linker.

alex: hmm, I don't love changing hoisting globally. Another pattern I used: add a tiny file import shim in the app that re-exports from the real dist path. e.g. src/libs/redwood-shim.js -> `export { default } from '../../node_modules/.pnpm/@redwood+sdk@0.12.0/node_modules/@redwood/sdk/dist/index.mjs'` then import from that shim in edge files. Ugly but works for quick demos.

nora: yeah ugly. Longer term we should document the recommended patterns for each runtime: Vercel/Next, Cloudflare Pages, Netlify Edge. Each has different resolver behavior.

ben: for the SDK package we might add a fallback export without conditional exports: `.mjs` as the main entry at the top-level in addition to exports. Eg: add "module": "dist/index.mjs" to package.json alongside exports.

alex: good idea. If we add "module" and ensure dist/index.mjs is present in the published tarball, that might reduce edge breakages. Opened an issue in the SDK repo to discuss: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/112 

docs-bot: Created doc task RDOC-203: "Edge runtimes + pnpm workspace resolution guide" (assignee: nora)

alex: plan: 1) try module + explicit types in next SDK release 2) add a short Troubleshooting note in DX onboarding about pnpm + edge 3) include a tiny repro in examples/mono-pnpm-edge. I'll drop a PR with the example later today and link the issue.

nora: thanks, please add which runtimes you tested and the pnpm version. I can draft the doc after reviewing the repro.

ben: happy to validate on our Netlify edge account too.

alex: thanks all :raised_hands:
